heroHeadline: Trump Claims 'Total Control' of Hormuz as Deadly Houthi Attack and US Blockade Strike Rock Shipping Lanes; Iran Dismisses Claim as 'Fake Intelligence'
heroSubtitle: Day 167 (August 13, 2026): With active strikes on Iranian territory still paused since Trump's July 16 pivot toward economic pressure, the standoff has centered on the Strait of Hormuz and its shipping lanes. Iran advanced a parliamentary bill (Aug 6) to bar US- and Israeli-linked vessels and separately reached a shipping-corridor framework with Oman (Aug 7-8) that still withholds a full reopening pending US concessions. On Aug 9, Khamenei's son and successor Mojtaba Khamenei appointed hardline former IRGC chief Mohsen Rezaei as Supreme National Security Council secretary, while the Pentagon urged contractors to ramp up munitions production amid stockpile concerns. Trump doubled down on sanctions-led 'Operation Economic Fury' (Aug 11) and, on Aug 10-11, introduced new demands for Iranian compensation and reparations. The standoff turned violent on Aug 11 (Day 165): a US Navy helicopter fired Hellfire missiles disabling the blockade-running cargo ship Vela Nova off Pakistan, while Houthi forces killed 6 people — 4 crew and 2 rescuers — in a 'double-tap' missile strike on the cargo ship Tihamah near Bab al-Mandeb, the first fatal Houthi attack on shipping since the war began. Oil prices rose on the incidents (Aug 12) as Hormuz reopening hopes dimmed further. Trump then declared the US has 'total control' of the strait and warned Iran could 'get blown away' (Aug 12), a claim Rezaei rejected — saying the strait stays closed until the blockade, sanctions, and US regional presence end and the Lebanon and Gaza wars conclude — and which Foreign Minister Araghchi dismissed on Aug 13 as based on 'fake intelligence,' warning of an 'even bigger miscalculation.' Shipping traffic remains near-collapsed at roughly 8 vessels/day versus a 130-140/day pre-war baseline. Brent crude stood at ~$88/bbl (Aug 13), up modestly from the July 16 trough. Washington's stated terms to end hostilities remain unchanged: Iran must declare all Hormuz channels open toll-free, halt attacks on shipping, and surrender its highly enriched uranium stockpile.
